subject: anatomy
title: Ventricular system, cerebrospinal fluid dynamics and meninges

steps.tx: Three protective **cranial meninges** envelop the central nervous system: the dura mater, arachnoid mater and pia mater. The tough fibrous dura has an outer periosteal layer and an inner meningeal layer. Infoldings of the meningeal layer form the falx cerebri, tentorium cerebelli, falx cerebelli and diaphragma sellae. The subarachnoid space lies between the arachnoid and pia, containing cerebrospinal fluid and major cerebral vessels.
steps.say: Three protective cranial meninges envelop the central nervous system: the dura mater, arachnoid mater and pia mater. The tough fibrous dura has an outer periosteal layer and an inner meningeal layer. Infoldings of the meningeal layer form the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli. The subarachnoid space lies between arachnoid and pia, containing cerebrospinal fluid and cerebral vessels.

steps.tx: The **ventricular system** comprises four interconnected fluid-filled cavities: two lateral ventricles in the cerebral hemispheres, the third ventricle in the midline diencephalon, and the fourth ventricle in the hindbrain. The lateral ventricles communicate with the third ventricle via the interventricular foramina of Monro. The third ventricle connects to the fourth ventricle through the narrow cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius in the midbrain.
steps.say: The ventricular system comprises four interconnected fluid-filled cavities: two lateral ventricles in the cerebral hemispheres, the third ventricle in the midline diencephalon, and the fourth ventricle in the hindbrain. The lateral ventricles communicate with the third ventricle via the foramina of Monro. The third connects to the fourth via the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of CSF circulation: produced by choroid plexus in the lateral ventricles, passes through the interventricular foramina to the third ventricle, the cerebral aqueduct to the fourth ventricle, exits through the median and lateral apertures into the subarachnoid space and is absorbed by arachnoid granulations into the superior sagittal sinus.
vis.caption: CSF is made in the ventricles and absorbed at the arachnoid granulations; a block anywhere upstream dilates the ventricles.

steps.tx: The **cerebrospinal fluid** is produced continuously by choroid plexuses in all four ventricles at approximately five hundred milliliters per day. Fluid exits the fourth ventricle into the subarachnoid space via three apertures: the median foramen of Magendie and two lateral foramina of Luschka. Remember: Magendie is Median; Luschka is Lateral. Fluid circulates around the brain and spinal cord, cushioned by subarachnoid cisterns.
steps.say: Cerebrospinal fluid is produced continuously by choroid plexuses in all four ventricles at approximately five hundred milliliters daily. Fluid exits the fourth ventricle into the subarachnoid space via three apertures: the median foramen of Magendie and two lateral foramina of Luschka. Remember: Magendie is Median, Luschka is Lateral. Fluid circulates around the neuraxis in subarachnoid cisterns.

steps.tx: Reabsorption of cerebrospinal fluid occurs through **arachnoid granulations** projecting into the superior sagittal sinus and other dural venous sinuses. Hydrocephalus results from an imbalance between production and absorption. Non-communicating hydrocephalus is caused by structural obstruction along the ventricular pathway, most often aqueductal stenosis. Communicating hydrocephalus arises from impaired arachnoid granulation reabsorption following subarachnoid hemorrhage or purulent meningitis.
steps.say: Reabsorption of cerebrospinal fluid occurs through arachnoid granulations projecting into the superior sagittal sinus. Hydrocephalus results from an imbalance between production and absorption. Non-communicating hydrocephalus is caused by structural obstruction such as aqueductal stenosis. Communicating hydrocephalus arises from impaired arachnoid granulation reabsorption following meningitis.
